correctness.rationale: The two mass coefficients at k=15 are independently computed as exact Fractions by `verify.py`, with h(15)<1<h(25). The general large-k proof uses a uniform convolution atom bound, Chebyshev pigeonhole lower atom bound, exact finite polynomial for h_k(k), and a proved termwise Bessel-series comparison. Numerical checks are not promoted to proofs.

originality.rationale: Inspected relevant original papers by Georghiou–Philippou–Saghafi (2013), Philippou (2014), Kwon–Philippou (2023), and three Mane (2023) preprints, plus Bessel source. Previously established root definition, monotonic first threshold, and the order-15 example are credited. The all-order asymptotic s_k~log(k)/k and second-order r_k expansion do not follow from their published statements; Mane’s numerical power-law fit is specifically not a proof and differs in asymptotic order. Residual risk of a further equivalent work remains; search results alone were not counted as proof of originality.
residual_risks: A separate independent priority assessment is not available; an equivalent treatment under compound-Poisson or stuttering-Poisson terminology beyond the inspected sources could exist.
The numerical finite-order power-fit discussion is not a theorem in the cited sources; no claim is made to new discovery of its k=15 counterexample or monotonicity of the true zero-mode threshold.
The exact finite-order threshold and modal index beyond the asymptotic regimes remain unknown from this proof.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves the growing-order first-zero-mode scale and the separate zero-versus-k crossing speed explicitly requested in Kwon and Philippou, explaining an entire eventual qualitative change and discriminating a true asymptotic from an earlier finite-data power fit. A sharp all-order asymptotic pair and their divergent ratio are mathematically motivated and not a mere low-order or routine numerical check.
